title: Your Voice Agent Doesn't Need a Frontier Model - Joel Allou & Ornella Bahidika, Microsoft
talk_summary: A Microsoft team built a live voice tutor on a small model (Haiku 4.5) by extracting all reasoning, lesson state, and 'what happens next' logic into an external state machine, leaving the model only to speak. They report ~900ms responses vs multi-second frontier-model latency, at the cost of writing strict scaffolding once in code.

takeaways.technique: Move decision logic out of the LLM into a deterministic state machine
takeaways.what_they_do: A code-level state machine owns lesson flow, mastery tracking, and next-step selection; the model receives a per-turn summary and only produces the utterance.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all of the thinking is extracted into a state machine
takeaways.numbers: ~900ms response on Haiku 4.5 vs multi-second on Opus 4.7

takeaways.technique: Pick the fastest model the latency budget allows, spend savings on scaffolding
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately chose the smallest capable model and invested engineering time in harness code rather than paying for frontier reasoning per turn.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Pick the fastest model that your latency budget allows and then spend the rest of your time actually building the scaffolding.

takeaways.technique: Pay scaffolding cost once in code, not per turn
takeaways.what_they_do: Strict rules and scenario handling live in code/state machine rather than being re-derived by the model on every turn.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you pay it once and in code, right? Not on every single turn.

takeaways.technique: Hand the model a per-turn summary instead of full history
takeaways.what_they_do: The external system tracks state and passes the model only a summary each turn, so the model never needs long context to stay coherent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they hand the model a summary every turn

takeaways.technique: Small models drift without strict rules; add explicit guardrails
takeaways.what_they_do: They acknowledge small models drift on long structures and compensate with strict rules in the harness.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if it doesn't have any scaffolding, tend to drift on long structure and really needs strict rules
